rationale: B wins because it turns the same four obvious lanes into sharper reporter questions. "Wise says stablecoin rails are cheaper — the open question is who keeps the savings" is a real tension; A's "cutting correspondent-banking fees is a margin story" jumps to the margin frame before proving who captures the savings. Same map, better discipline: B tells the founder which facts will make reporters bite instead of merely admiring the launch from four angles.
gaps_in_A: "For a profitable public payments company, cutting correspondent-banking fees is a margin story" assumes Wise's unit economics improve; the update says the product is faster and cheaper than correspondent banking, not that Wise keeps the spread.

"One of the biggest cross-border payment networks" is probably defensible, but it is still a ranking claim hanging on one supplied number: "over £30B" per quarter. Needs external context before a reporter repeats it.
"direct shot at correspondent banking's toll booth" is vivid, but a little over-cranked. The release supports a cheaper alternative; it does not prove incumbents are actually under threat yet.

"Next step: journalist-fit-check" skips the gating problem. Before names, the founder needs the unnamed stablecoin, partner, launch markets, and cost baseline or several reporters will stall immediately.
gaps_in_B: "which bank fees and float revenue get squeezed" stretches past the supplied update. Bank fees are fair; float revenue needs sourcing or it becomes banker fan fiction.

"stablecoin settlement is crossing into regulated, mainstream B2B money movement" is a strong category claim from one launch. It works as a hypothesis, but needs comparable examples before it becomes a trend sentence.
"Not for trade press, policy desks, or crypto outlets" in the equities angle is too absolute. A serious payments trade reporter could still care about pricing and margin effects.
"SWIFT-rail economics" is plausible beat language, but the update names correspondent banking, not SWIFT. Keep SWIFT as a reporter context, not a factual claim from the announcement.
